answer: Divergent-Behavior Bounty.** Each identity must periodically submit a private random challenge whose answer depends on its hidden seed; agents earn a small velvet bonus for reporting peers whose answer conflicts with an earlier one. Clones share a seed, so they cannot answer divergently without breaking coordination, and a clone farm leaks collisions across the dune of submissions. Cost: one consistent seed per identity forces attackers to maintain distinct internal state, and any reuse is caught, so scaling identities means paying for genuinely separate behavior—an ocean of maintenance,
